title: Council directs proactive termite management program
subtitle: Farmhouse for health care recruits, Habitat for Humanity rezoning, pumping station study, parking enforcement and 2022 surplus
overview: Council voted to move toward a proactive termite management program, directing staff to issue a negotiated Request for Proposal {{vote:m4}}. Three delegations had urged this approach. Staff said the cost is unknown until proposals arrive, and that $200,000 is already set aside.

To support physician recruitment, Council approved use of the Township-owned farmhouse at 965 Gartshore Street, Fergus, as accommodation for health care professionals {{vote:m2}}. Council also rezoned 465 Garafraxa St. W. to allow a Habitat for Humanity stacked townhouse development {{vote:m5}}, and awarded the Union Street sewage pumping station expansion environmental assessment to MTE Consultants Inc. {{vote:m9}}.

Council moved the 2022 operating surplus of $31,130 to the general capital reserve {{vote:m10}}. It also appointed municipal law enforcement officers so County property staff can enforce parking for winter maintenance {{vote:m7}}, and adopted the joint Accessibility Advisory Committee terms of reference {{vote:m8}}. Council heard a Fire Master Plan update and approved a noise by-law exemption for a wedding reception {{vote:m6}}. Two notices of motion were given on a disc golf course and cannabis retail.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to release a negotiated Request for Proposal to start a proactive termite management program, subject to successful award.
Council approved using the Township-owned farmhouse at 965 Gartshore Street, Fergus, as accommodation for health care professionals.
Council approved the zoning amendment and gave three readings to the by-law, allowing a stacked townhouse development for Habitat for Humanity.
Council awarded the Municipal Class Environmental Assessment to MTE Consultants Inc. at an upset limit of $124,711.60 excluding HST, and updated project funding.
Council received the 2022 operating results and transferred the $31,130 surplus to the general capital reserve.
Council authorized a by-law appointing municipal law enforcement officers to enforce the Parking By-law, at the County's request for winter maintenance.
Council adopted the County's joint committee terms of reference and named the Clerk as staff member attending meetings.

debate: Termite delegates argued that homeowners cannot control termites beyond their own properties, so only a coordinated, block-by-block approach would work. They said individual homeowners have already spent thousands of dollars. One delegate suggested staying flexible because a new treatment product may soon reach the Canadian market.

Staff set out two options: continue the passive education approach, or pursue a proactive program. Staff said a program could cost about a million dollars over several years, based on a neighbouring township. It would be funded from taxation or other funds, not building permit money, and the RFP would ask vendors to propose the scope and include project management.

Councillors asked how residents learn whether they are in a termite zone, what exit points the contract would allow, and whether a stronger termite by-law was needed. Staff said the survey is on the Township website, and that the RFP would aim to limit long-term obligations if results fall short.

On health care recruitment, a health care alliance representative said short-term housing for locums and students is the most pressing recruitment need. Staff said the farmhouse is a temporary solution while the future operations centre is designed. One councillor asked whether it could serve as a pilot for other properties.

On operating results, a councillor asked whether the surplus depended on unfilled positions. Staff said some vacancies helped, and that the positions are already built into next year's budget. Another councillor said the lines behind the surplus deserve closer reflection.
